Seeded workloads become queued jobs, the scheduler picks the next job by policy, and placement chooses a logical worker. Reservation commits capacity inside a MySQL transaction that locks the worker row, so concurrent jobs can never over-allocate it. The job then runs as one locked-down container limited to exactly that reservation, and recording its result releases the capacity in a single transaction. The dashboard reads job and resource records from MySQL. Panels refresh independently, and the job table shows recent updates.
